newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha stable to weaker in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha stable to weaker in quiet trade.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices were stable to weaker in dull Monday trade, as most market participants maintained a low profile, traders said.

Bids for open-spec naphtha for first-half February were heard at $223.00, with offers at $224.00. Second-half January was assessed at $224.50/226.50. It changed hands at $226.25 in late trade on Friday.
Also on Friday, second-half February was sold from a western trader to a Japanese trading house at $223.00.
The one-month spread from first-half January was talked at plus $4.00/5.00, compared to Friday's plus $3.50/4.50.
A delay in the start-up of LG-Caltex Oil Corp's 220,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) crude distillation unit (CDU) has already been factored into the regional naphtha market, traders said.
"We expected the delay as they (LG-Caltex) were in the market last week looking for prompt cargoes," one dealer said.

The South Korean firm said on Monday that it delayed feeding crude oil to its new CDU after finding a defect in the unit's column. It was unclear when the unit could resume operations, the oil company added.
The unit was originally scheduled to reach full production on November 23. --Tokyo Energy Desk +81-3-3432-8837
